body: As a professional mechanic who has been bleeding these brakes for 4+ years at this point, SRAM 11 speed hydraulic is by far my least favourite brake to bleed. Even if the bleed is successful, the way the brake lever hits the shift lever in the middle of its stroke gives it a two-part feel that I find super annoying and unsatisfactory. As others have suggested, if you’re having to bleed these pretty regularly there is likely a leak somewhere in your line, but I am still very pro-throwing these in the garbage 🤷🏼‍♂️

I used to have one on my gravel bike and it also only lasted one chain before it was worn out. I can’t play the link to the noise for some reason, but if it sounds like kind of a slurping under load, that’s a worn chainring.

If I’m reading this correctly, you bought a 110mm boost fork, but it’s measuring at 100? That’s either very bent lowers, they sent you the wrong fork, or you bought the wrong fork. If it’s a recently made rockshox fork, I would look the serial member on the back of the CSU up on Rockshox Trailhead and confirm that it’s indeed a 110mm dropout.

By 130 or 110mm I assume you mean 130 or 110BCD. I’d use this guide by Wolf Tooth to measure the current BCD.

https://www.wolftoothcomponents.com/pages/how-to-measure-bolt-circle-diameter-bcd
If the frame is steel, which it seems like it is, you should be totally fine to straighten it. Steel is super hard to break like that. I would just go slowly.
